portal_description:
The strongimcv packages provide Trusted Network Connect's (TNC) architecture
support. They include support for a TNC client and server (IF-TNCCS), Integrity
Measurement  Collector (IMC) and Integrity Measurement Verifier (IMV) message
exchange (IF-M), as well as an interface between IMC/IMV and a TNC client/server
(IF-IMC and IF-IMV). They also include PTS-based IMC/IMV for TPM-based remote
attestation, SWID IMC/IMV, and OS IMC/IMV.

The strongimcv packages have been upgraded to upstream version 5.2.0, which
provides a number of bug fixes and enhancements over the previous version.
(BZ#1120371)

This update also fixes the following bugs:

* Previously, the strongimcv policy script used a hard-coded name for the
strongimcv executable, which did not correspond with the executable name in Red
Hat Enterprise Linux 7. As a consequence, running the strongimcv policy manager
in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 failed. This update modifies the policy script to
use a flexible executable name, which prevents the described problem.
(BZ#1144511)

* Due to threading incompatibility with the strongimcv OpenSSL plug-in, the
wpa_supplicant program terminated unexpectedly with a segmentation fault after a
TNC negotiation finished if wpa_supplicant was running along with strongimcv.
With this update, the strongimcv OpenSSL plug-in has been update to be
thread-compatible with wpa_supplicant, and wpa_supplicant no longer crashes
after TNC negotiations. (BZ#1144524)

* Prior to this update, the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol client of
strongimcv was not compatible with the 64-bit PowerPC microarchitecture. As a
consequence, using the "strongimcv pt-tls-client" command on a 64-bit PowerPC
machine failed. This update addresses the compatibility problems and "strongimcv
pt-tls-client" now works as expected on 64-bit PowerPC machines. (BZ#1179330)

Users of strongimcv are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix
these bugs and add these enhancements.
